info.name: LedgerOne - Authorization
info.description:
Authorization module (Role, Permission, Role<->Permission, User<->Role) API collection (Create, Get, Update, Retire, List Role; List Permission; Assign, Remove, List Role Permissions; Assign, Remove, List User Roles). Reflects the implementation exactly as shipped in apps/api/src/shared/authorization, mounted at /api/v1/authorization (module-registry.ts).

Design note (JWT required, but no X-Tenant-Id validation path for Permission): Permission is platform-owned reference data (06_DATABASE_STANDARDS.md MT-005, list-permissions.controller.ts's own comment) so GET /permissions declares no X-Tenant-Id requirement -- but every /api/v1/authorization/* route, Permission included, still sits behind jwt-auth.middleware.ts (verified: a Permission request with no Authorization header still 401s with AUTH_MISSING_TOKEN). Every other route in this module (Role, Role Permissions, User Roles) requires X-Tenant-Id like every other tenant-owned module.

KNOWN GAP #1 -- Permission has no seed data and no create endpoint at all: apps/api/src/database/seeds has no permissions.seed.ts anywhere in the repo, and this module exposes no HTTP route to create a Permission either (index.ts mounts only GET /permissions -- no POST). This means GET /permissions returns an empty array on a fresh local dev DB, and the entire 'Role Permissions' folder's success/duplicate-grant test cases CANNOT pass unless at least one row already exists in the permissions table, inserted directly outside this collection (SQL or Prisma Studio -- there is no HTTP way to create one). An illustrative (NOT executed) example insert shape:
  INSERT INTO permissions (id, uuid, permission_key, module_name, resource, action, description, created_at, updated_at)
  VALUES (1, UUID(), 'authorization.role.view', 'authorization', 'role', 'VIEW', 'View Roles', NOW(), NOW());
See the {{permissionKey}} collection variable (defaults to an empty string) -- fill it in manually with a real permission_key from your local dev DB before running the 'Role Permissions' folder's success/duplicate cases. Without it, those two requests will observe the real (and equally valid) 404 AUTHZ_PERMISSION_NOT_FOUND gap behavior instead, which the requests' own test scripts detect and report on explicitly rather than failing silently.

KNOWN GAP #2 -- User<->Role needs a real User this module doesn't own: Authorization does not own User (FK-002, a cross-module reference to User Management's users.uuid, mirrored from assign-role.service.ts's own comment). The 'User Roles' folder's requests use a {{userUuid}} collection variable (defaults to an empty string) that must be filled in manually with a real User's uuid from your own local dev DB (e.g. one created via the User Management module, or the dev seed's fixture user in apps/api/src/database/seeds/development/users.seed.ts) before running that folder -- mirroring how Currency's own collection documents manual-fixture requirements the API itself cannot satisfy.

Design note (repeatable Role-name generation): Role.name is unique per tenant (00_BUSINESS_RULES.md Ch.11.8/AUTHZ_DUPLICATE_ROLE_NAME) and there is no delete endpoint for Role at all (only the one-way Active -> Retired lifecycle transition), so repeated Newman runs cannot rely on a prior run's rows being gone. A collection-level pre-request script derives two distinct Role names from Date.now() (mirroring Currency.postman_collection.json's own Date.now()-based generation trick, adapted for a name field instead of a 3-letter ISO code) once per Newman invocation, making cross-run collisions practically impossible without needing manual cleanup between runs. Test data (Roles created by this collection) has no HTTP delete path to clean up via the API itself; if a permanent record is undesired, delete the rows directly via SQL after a verification pass.

Run order for a full pass, top to bottom: every Role request before the Role Permissions and User Roles folders ({{roleUuid}}/{{secondRoleUuid}} must both be set, by 'Create Role - Success' and 'Create Second Role - Success', before either folder runs); the 'User Roles' folder's 'Assign Role to User - Rejects Retired Role (Not Assignable)' case depends on the Role folder's 'Retire Role - Success' request having already retired {{secondRoleUuid}}.
